summary: This note is a wiki-style overview of the United Kingdom's history in the Eurovision Song Contest. It states that the UK has competed 60 times, first in the 1957 contest and every year since 1959, and has won five times. It also notes the UK's place among the 'Big 5' automatically qualifying countries and the BBC's role in broadcasting and selecting its entries.
one_line: Overview of the United Kingdom's 60 Eurovision Song Contest appearances, five wins, and BBC role.
key_facts: The United Kingdom has participated in the Eurovision Song Contest 60 times.
The United Kingdom first participated in the second Eurovision Song Contest in 1957.
The United Kingdom has entered every Eurovision Song Contest since 1959.
The United Kingdom has won the Eurovision Song Contest a total of five times.
Along with Sweden, the United Kingdom is one of only two countries with Eurovision victories in four different decades.
The United Kingdom is one of the 'Big 5' countries, along with France, Germany, Italy and Spain.
The Big 5 countries are automatically allowed to participate in the final.
The Big 5 are the five biggest financial contributors to the European Broadcasting Union (EBU).
The British public broadcaster, the BBC, broadcasts the Eurovision Song Contest each year.
The BBC organises the national selection for the United Kingdom's entry.
